title: Cerebellar tDCS in Schizophrenia
official: Non-invasive Cerebellar Stimulation and Predictive Coding in Schizophrenia
summary:
The goal of this study is to learn if non-invasive brain stimulation works to change behavioral and brain-related measures associated with delusions in patients with schizophrenia. The main questions the study aims to answer are:

* Does non-invasive brain stimulation improve performance on tasks that have been shown to be associated with delusion severity?
* Does non-invasive brain stimulation change neural measures from tasks that have been shown to be associated with delusion severity?

Researchers will compare active brain stimulation to sham (a process that produces similar sensations to active stimulation but does not produce the same changes in brain activity) to see if non-invasive brain stimulation works to change behavioral and brain-related measures associated with delusions in patients with schizophrenia.

Participants will:

* Complete tasks and brain recording after sham.
* Complete tasks and brain recording after active stimulation.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* age 18 - 49
* meet the Structured Clinical Interview for DSM-V (SCID) diagnostic criteria for schizophrenia or schizoaffective disorder
* endorse a minimum of mild delusions (score of 3+) as measured by the Brief Psychiatric Rating Scale (BPRS)

Exclusion Criteria:

* changes in antipsychotic medication in the month prior to study participation or anticipated changes in the next month
* a clinically significant head injury or neurological disease
* receiving noninvasive brain stimulation treatment in the past three months
* IQ less than 70
* unmedicated individuals in acute exacerbation that would require immediate hospitalization or treatment and those that report medication non-compliance over the past month (e.g., indicate they never started medications that they were prescribed or stopping taking prescribed medication)
* personal history of seizure
